title: Diplomatik va yumshoq til
goal_uz: Dars oxirida tanqidni yumshatasiz, rad etishni muloyim va aniq ifodalaysiz, bilvosita iltimoslarni to‘g‘ri grammatika bilan tuzasiz va suhbatdoshning obro‘sini saqlab, qiyin vaziyatlarni hal qilasiz.

scenes.title: Diplomatik va yumshoq til
board: Diplomatic language
Tanqid · rad etish · bilvosita iltimos · obro‘ni saqlash
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda izchil tarjimani o‘rgandik. Bugun har bir tarjimon va har bir rahbarga kerak bo‘ladigan narsa — diplomatiya. Xafa qilmasdan tanqid qilish, xafa qilmasdan rad etish va buyruq ohangisiz iltimos qilish mumkinmi? Ingliz tilida buning uchun boy vositalar bor. Dars oxirida siz tanqidni yumshatasiz, „yo‘q“ ni muloyim aytasiz, bilvosita iltimos tuzasiz va suhbatdoshingizning obro‘sini saqlaysiz. Esda tuting: diplomatik til yolg‘on gapirish emas. Siz haqiqatni aytasiz, faqat tinglovchi uni eshitishga tayyor bo‘ladigan shaklda.
scenes.say: Hello again. Last lesson was about interpreting. Today we look at something every interpreter and every manager needs: diplomacy. How do you criticise without hurting, refuse without offending, and ask for something without sounding bossy? English has a rich toolkit for exactly this.
scenes.say_uz: Yana salom. O‘tgan dars tarjima haqida edi. Bugun har bir tarjimon va rahbarga kerak narsani ko‘ramiz: diplomatiyani. Xafa qilmasdan qanday tanqid qilish, xafa qilmasdan qanday rad etish va buyruq ohangisiz qanday iltimos qilish mumkin? Ingliz tilida aynan shu uchun boy vositalar bor.

scenes.title: Tanqidni yumshatish
board: hedges: a bit · somewhat · slightly · rather
I wonder if… · It might be worth… · I would suggest…
positive – issue – solution
not quite · could be clearer

examples.t: The summary is a bit long, so it might be worth trimming the second section.
examples.uz: Xulosa biroz uzun, shuning uchun ikkinchi bo‘limni qisqartirish foydali bo‘lishi mumkin.

examples.t: I would suggest making the conclusion a little clearer.
examples.uz: Xulosani biroz aniqroq qilishni tavsiya qilardim.

examples.t: This is not quite what we were expecting.
examples.uz: Bu biz kutgan narsa emas.

scenes.say_native: Tanqidni yumshatish uchun odamni emas, muammoni tasvirlang va tilni „hedge“ qiling, ya’ni kuchini pasaytiring. „A bit“, „slightly“, „somewhat“ — biroz, ozgina — kuchni kamaytiradi. „I wonder if…“, „it might be worth…“, „I would suggest…“ — harakatga undaydi, buyurmaydi. Ingliz tilida kamaytirib aytish ham keng tarqalgan: „not quite right“ aslida „noto‘g‘ri“ ma’nosini bildiradi. Yaxshi tuzilma: avval ijobiy, keyin muammo, keyin yechim. Masalan: „The structure is clear. It is a bit long, so it might be worth trimming the second section.“ O‘zbek tilida „yaxshi, lekin…“ ko‘p ishlatiladi, ingliz tilida ham shu, faqat „but“ ni haddan ortiq qo‘llamang.
scenes.say: To soften criticism, describe the issue, not the person, and hedge your language. Hedges such as a bit, slightly and somewhat reduce the force. Suggestions with I wonder if, it might be worth and I would suggest invite action rather than demand it. Many speakers also use understatement: not quite right means wrong. A good frame is praise, issue, solution.
scenes.say_uz: Tanqidni yumshatish uchun odamni emas, muammoni tasvirlang va tilni hedge qiling. A bit, slightly, somewhat kuchni kamaytiradi. I wonder if, it might be worth, I would suggest harakatga undaydi. Kamaytirib aytish ham keng tarqalgan: not quite right aslida noto‘g‘ri degani. Yaxshi tuzilma: ijobiy, muammo, yechim.

scenes.title: Xato: shaxsga qaratilgan tanqid
board: ✗ You always write messy reports
✓ The report could be better organised
✗ This is wrong. / ✓ I am not sure this is quite right

examples.t: The data in the second table does not seem to match the text.
examples.uz: Ikkinchi jadvaldagi ma’lumot matn bilan mos kelmayotganga o‘xshaydi.

examples.t: I may have missed something, but could we check this figure?
examples.uz: Men nimanidir o‘tkazib yuborgan bo‘lishim mumkin, lekin bu raqamni tekshirsak bo‘ladimi?

scenes.say_native: Qo‘pollikning uch odatiy shakli bor. Birinchi: shaxsga hujum — „You always write messy reports“. Ikkinchi: „always“, „never“ kabi mutlaq so‘zlar, ular bahsni qo‘zg‘atadi. Uchinchi: quruq hukm — „This is wrong“. Buning o‘rniga ishga e’tibor qarating: „The report could be better organised“. „Seems“ yoki „appears“ ishlating: „This does not seem to match the text“ — bu matn bilan mos kelmayotganga o‘xshaydi. Boshqa odamga yo‘l qoldiring: „I may be missing something, but could we check this figure?“ Bu yerda siz ham xato qilishingiz mumkinligini tan olasiz, bu esa suhbatni hujumdan hamkorlikka aylantiradi. O‘zbek tilida „sizda xato bor“ deyilishi ham qattiq eshitiladi, shuning uchun bu tamoyil ikki tilda ham ishlaydi.
scenes.say: Bluntness has three typical forms. First, attacking the person: you always write messy reports. Second, absolute words such as always and never, which invite an argument. Third, flat statements like this is wrong. Instead, focus on the work, use seems or appears, and leave room for the other person: I may be missing something, but could we check this?
scenes.say_uz: Qo‘pollikning uch shakli bor: shaxsga hujum, always va never kabi mutlaq so‘zlar, quruq hukm. Buning o‘rniga ishga e’tibor qarating, seems yoki appears ishlating va boshqa odamga yo‘l qoldiring. Siz ham xato qilishingiz mumkinligini tan olsangiz, suhbat hamkorlikka aylanadi.

scenes.title: Mashq: tanqidni yumshating
board: 1) Your presentation is boring.
2) You never listen in meetings.
3) This budget is wrong.
scenes.say_native: Mana, uchta qo‘pol gapni yumshating. Birinchisi: „Your presentation is boring“. Ikkinchisi: „You never listen in meetings“. Uchinchisi: „This budget is wrong“. Ishga e’tibor qarating, hedge ishlating va imkon bo‘lsa, taklif qo‘shing. Shaxsga emas, muammoga qarating. Javoblaringizni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Soften these three blunt sentences. One: your presentation is boring. Two: you never listen in meetings. Three: this budget is wrong. Focus on the work, use hedges, and add a suggestion where you can.
scenes.say_uz: Uchta qo‘pol gapni yumshating. Taqdimotingiz zerikarli. Siz majlislarda hech qachon tinglamaysiz. Bu byudjet noto‘g‘ri. Ishga e’tibor qarating, hedge ishlating va taklif qo‘shing.

scenes.title: Javoblar: yumshatilgan tanqid
board: The presentation could be a bit more engaging.
I have noticed some ideas getting missed in meetings.
The budget does not seem to add up.

examples.t: The presentation might be more engaging with a couple of examples.
examples.uz: Taqdimot bir-ikki misol bilan qiziqarliroq bo‘lishi mumkin.

scenes.say_native: Mumkin variantlar: „The presentation could be a bit more engaging, and a couple of examples might help.“ „I have noticed that a few points get missed in meetings, so perhaps we could recap together afterwards.“ „The budget does not seem to add up, so could we go through the figures?“ Har bir variant ishni nishonga oladi va keyingi qadamni taklif qiladi. „Never listen“ ni yumshatganda „I have noticed“ — „sezdimki“ ni ishlatdik va aniq holatga o‘tdik. Mutlaq so‘z o‘rniga konkret kuzatuv bo‘lsa, suhbatdosh o‘zini himoya qilishga shoshilmaydi.
scenes.say: Possible versions. The presentation could be a bit more engaging, and a couple of examples might help. I have noticed that a few points get missed in meetings, so perhaps we could recap together afterwards. The budget does not seem to add up, so could we go through the figures? Each version targets the work and offers a next step.
scenes.say_uz: Mumkin variantlar. Taqdimot biroz qiziqarliroq bo‘lishi mumkin, bir-ikki misol yordam berardi. Majlislarda ba’zi fikrlar o‘tkazib yuborilayotganini sezdim, balki keyin birga takrorlarmiz. Byudjet mos kelmayotganga o‘xshaydi, raqamlarni ko‘rib chiqsak bo‘ladimi?

scenes.title: Muloyim rad etish
board: I am afraid I cannot…
I would love to, but…
Unfortunately, we are unable to…
What I can do is… · Would it help if…?

examples.t: I would love to help, but I am fully booked this week.
examples.uz: Yordam berishni juda istardim, lekin bu hafta band bo‘lib turibman.

examples.t: Unfortunately, we are unable to offer a discount at this stage.
examples.uz: Afsuski, hozirgi bosqichda chegirma taklif qila olmaymiz.

examples.t: I cannot do Friday, but what I can do is send it on Monday.
examples.uz: Juma kuni qilolmayman, lekin dushanba kuni yubora olaman.

scenes.say_native: Muloyim rad etishning uch qismi bor: yumshoq boshlanish, qisqa sabab va muqobil. Boshlanish: „I am afraid…“, „I would love to, but…“, „Unfortunately…“. Sabab qisqa va rost bo‘lsin. Keyin nima qila olishingizga o‘ting: „What I can do is…“ yoki „Would it help if…?“. Diqqat: „I am afraid“ bu yerda „qo‘rqaman“ degani emas, faqat muloyimlik formulasi: „I am afraid I cannot attend“ — afsuski, qatnasha olmayman. O‘zbek tilida „yo‘q, bo‘lmaydi“ qisqa va to‘g‘ri, inglizchada esa uni yumshoq boshlanish va muqobil bilan o‘rash odat. Shunda rad etilgan odam ham yordam topganini his qiladi.
scenes.say: A polite refusal has three parts: a soft opening, a brief reason, and an alternative. Openers include I am afraid, I would love to but, and unfortunately. Keep the reason short and truthful. Then turn to what you can do: what I can do is, or would it help if. Note that I am afraid here is only a polite formula, not a statement of fear.
scenes.say_uz: Muloyim rad etishning uch qismi: yumshoq boshlanish, qisqa sabab va muqobil. Boshlanishlar: I am afraid, I would love to but, unfortunately. Sabab qisqa va rost bo‘lsin. Keyin nima qila olishingizni ayting. I am afraid bu yerda qo‘rquv emas, muloyimlik formulasi.

scenes.title: Xato: to‘g‘ri “no” va ortiqcha uzr
board: ✗ No, impossible.
✓ I am afraid that is not possible at the moment, but…
✗ I am so, so sorry, I feel terrible, please forgive me…

examples.t: I will have to decline, I am afraid.
examples.uz: Afsuski, rad etishimga to‘g‘ri keladi.

examples.t: That does not fit our schedule, but we could look at May.
examples.uz: Bu bizning jadvalimizga to‘g‘ri kelmaydi, lekin may oyini ko‘rib chiqsak bo‘ladi.

scenes.say_native: Ikki chet muammo tug‘diradi. Yalang‘och „No, impossible“ dushmanlarcha eshitiladi. Cheksiz uzr esa zaif ko‘rinadi va qarshi tomonni bosimni davom ettirishga undaydi. Aniq „yo‘q“ ni iliq so‘zlar bilan, bir marta ayting va variant taklif qiling: „I am afraid that is not possible at the moment, but we could look at May.“ „Maybe“ demang, agar aslida „yo‘q“ demoqchi bo‘lsangiz: soxta umid hammaning vaqtini yo‘qotadi. Muloyim degani noaniq degani emas. O‘zbek madaniyatida ba’zan rad etish „ko‘ramiz“ deb aytiladi, ingliz ish muhitida esa „we will see“ ko‘pincha „ha“ deb tushuniladi, shuning uchun aniqroq bo‘ling.
scenes.say: Two extremes cause problems. A bare no, impossible sounds hostile. An endless apology sounds weak and can make the other side keep pushing. Give a clear no in warm words, once, then offer an option. Do not say maybe if you mean no, because a false hope wastes everyone's time. And remember that polite does not mean unclear.
scenes.say_uz: Ikki chet muammo tug‘diradi. Yalang‘och no dushmanlarcha eshitiladi, cheksiz uzr esa zaif ko‘rinadi. Aniq yo‘qni iliq so‘zlar bilan bir marta ayting va variant taklif qiling. Agar yo‘q demoqchi bo‘lsangiz, maybe demang. Muloyim degani noaniq degani emas.

scenes.title: Mashq: muloyim rad eting
board: 1) A client asks for a 30% discount
2) A colleague asks you to work on Saturday
3) Give a reason + an alternative
scenes.say_native: Ikki vaziyatda muloyim rad eting. Birinchisi: mijoz o‘ttiz foiz chegirma so‘raydi, siz ko‘pi bilan o‘n foiz bera olasiz. Ikkinchisi: hamkasb sizdan shanba kuni ishlashni so‘raydi, lekin sizda oilaviy majburiyat bor. Yumshoq boshlanish, qisqa sabab va muqobil ishlating. Javoblaringizni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Decline politely in two situations. First, a client asks for a thirty per cent discount, and you can offer at most ten. Second, a colleague asks you to work on Saturday, but you have a family commitment. Use a soft opener, a short reason and an alternative.
scenes.say_uz: Ikki vaziyatda muloyim rad eting. Mijoz o‘ttiz foiz chegirma so‘raydi, siz ko‘pi bilan o‘n foiz bera olasiz. Hamkasb shanba kuni ishlashni so‘raydi, sizda oilaviy majburiyat bor. Yumshoq boshlanish, qisqa sabab va muqobil ishlating.

scenes.title: Javoblar: rad etish
board: I am afraid thirty per cent is beyond what we can offer; I can do ten.
I would love to help, but I have a family commitment. I could cover Friday evening instead.

examples.t: I am afraid thirty per cent is beyond our range, but we could offer ten.
examples.uz: Afsuski, o‘ttiz foiz bizning imkoniyatimizdan tashqarida, lekin o‘n foiz taklif qila olamiz.

scenes.say_native: Namunaviy javoblar: „I am afraid thirty per cent is beyond what we can offer, but we could do ten per cent on a larger order.“ Va: „I would love to help, but I have a family commitment on Saturday. I could cover some of the work on Friday evening instead.“ Ikkalasi yumshoq boshlanadi, qisqa sabab keltiradi va muqobil taklif qiladi. Birinchi javobda „on a larger order“ — kattaroq buyurtmada, shart ham qo‘shildi, bu muzokarada yaxshi usul. Bu javoblarda „no“ so‘zining o‘zi yo‘q, lekin ma’no aniq: rad etildi.
scenes.say: Model replies. I am afraid thirty per cent is beyond what we can offer, but we could do ten per cent on a larger order. And: I would love to help, but I have a family commitment on Saturday. I could cover some of the work on Friday evening instead. Both start softly, give a short reason and propose an alternative.
scenes.say_uz: Namunaviy javoblar. Afsuski, o‘ttiz foiz bizning imkoniyatimizdan tashqarida, lekin kattaroq buyurtmada o‘n foiz bera olamiz. Yordam berishni istardim, lekin shanba kuni oilaviy majburiyatim bor, buning o‘rniga juma kechqurun ishning bir qismini bajara olaman.

scenes.title: Bilvosita iltimoslar
board: Could you…? · Would you mind + -ing?
I was wondering if you could…
Would it be possible to…?
I would be grateful if you could…

examples.t: Would you mind sending me the agenda?
examples.uz: Kun tartibini menga yuborib bera olasizmi?

examples.t: I was wondering if you could review this draft.
examples.uz: Shu qoralamani ko‘rib chiqa olasizmi, deb o‘ylagan edim.

examples.t: Would it be possible to move the deadline to Thursday?
examples.uz: Muddatni payshanbaga ko‘chirish mumkinmi?

scenes.say_native: Bilvosita iltimos buyruqni savolga aylantirib, bosimni kamaytiradi. „Could you…?“, „would you…?“ — standart. „Would you mind“ dan keyin fe’lning -ing shakli keladi: „Would you mind sending me the agenda?“ „I was wondering if you could…“ — yanada ehtiyotkor, o‘tgan zamon masofa va muloyimlik qo‘shadi. „Would it be possible to…?“ — tashkilotga murojaat uchun yaxshi. „I would be grateful if you could…“ — rasmiy yozuvga mos. Uzbek tilida iltimos „iltimos“ so‘zi va fe’l shakli bilan ifodalanadi, inglizchada esa asosiy yumshatuvchi — modal fe’l va savol shakli. Qanchalik rasmiy bo‘lsangiz, shuncha uzunroq qolip tanlaysiz.
scenes.say: Indirect requests reduce pressure by turning a command into a question. Could you and would you are standard. Would you mind is followed by the -ing form. I was wondering if is more tentative, and the past tense adds distance and politeness. Would it be possible to is good for requests to an institution. I would be grateful if you could suits formal writing.
scenes.say_uz: Bilvosita iltimos buyruqni savolga aylantirib, bosimni kamaytiradi. Could you va would you standart. Would you mind dan keyin -ing shakli keladi. I was wondering if yanada ehtiyotkor. Would it be possible to tashkilotga murojaat uchun yaxshi. I would be grateful if you could rasmiy yozuvga mos.

scenes.title: Xato: would you mind to
board: ✗ Would you mind to send it?
✓ Would you mind sending it?
✗ Can you give me the report now!

examples.t: Would you mind if I opened the window?
examples.uz: Oynani ochsam, xalaqit bermaydimi?

examples.t: Could you possibly give me a few more minutes?
examples.uz: Menga yana bir necha daqiqa bera olasizmi?

scenes.say_native: Eng ko‘p uchraydigan grammatik xato — „Would you mind to send“. „Mind“ dan keyin -ing: „Would you mind sending“. Ruxsat so‘rasangiz, o‘tgan zamon: „Would you mind if I opened the window?“ Javobga e’tibor bering: „Would you mind…?“ ga „No, not at all“ degan javob „yo‘q, qarshi emasman“, ya’ni „ha, mumkin“ degani. O‘zbek tilidagi „xalaqit bermaydimi?“ ga „yo‘q“ deyilganidek. Buyruq-undov ham yaxshi emas: „Can you give me the report now!“ shoshiltirayotgandek eshitiladi. Shoshilinch bo‘lsa, sababini ayting: „I need it before the meeting at three, so could you possibly send it by two?“
scenes.say: The most frequent grammar error is would you mind to send. After mind, use the -ing form: would you mind sending. If you ask permission, use the past: would you mind if I opened the window? Remember too that the answer no, not at all means yes, you may. And avoid the urgent bare command with an exclamation, as in can you give me the report now.
scenes.say_uz: Eng ko‘p uchraydigan xato: would you mind to send. Mind dan keyin -ing shakli keladi. Ruxsat so‘rasangiz, o‘tgan zamon: would you mind if I opened the window. No, not at all degan javob ha, mumkin degani. Shoshilinch bo‘lsa, sababini ayting.

scenes.title: Mashq: iltimosni qayta yozing
board: 1) Send me the file.
2) Move your car.
3) Give me an answer today.
scenes.say_native: Uchta buyruqni muloyim, bilvosita iltimosga aylantiring. Birinchisi: „Send me the file“. Ikkinchisi: „Move your car“. Uchinchisi: „Give me an answer today“. Har biriga bittadan qolip ishlating: „would you mind“, „I was wondering if“, „would it be possible“. Fe’l shakliga e’tibor bering.
scenes.say: Rewrite three commands as polite, indirect requests. Send me the file. Move your car. Give me an answer today. Use would you mind, I was wondering if, and would it be possible, one in each.
scenes.say_uz: Uchta buyruqni muloyim, bilvosita iltimosga aylantiring. Faylni menga yuboring. Mashinangizni siljiting. Bugun javob bering. Har biriga would you mind, I was wondering if va would it be possible dan bittadan ishlating.

scenes.title: Javoblar: iltimoslar
board: Would you mind sending me the file?
I was wondering if you could move your car.
Would it be possible to have an answer today?

examples.t: Would it be possible to have an answer by the end of today?
examples.uz: Bugun kun oxirigacha javob olish mumkinmi?

scenes.say_native: Mumkin javoblar: „Would you mind sending me the file?“ — „mind“ dan keyin „sending“. „I was wondering if you could move your car, as it is blocking the entrance“ — „was wondering“ o‘tgan zamonda, sabab ham qo‘shildi. „Would it be possible to have an answer by the end of today?“ — „to have“ dan keyin ot birikmasi. Sabab qo‘shish iltimosni yanada muloyim va oqilona qiladi. Agar uchala gapingizda ham modal yoki savol shakli bo‘lsa va bosim yo‘q bo‘lsa, topshiriq bajarilgan.
scenes.say: Possible answers. Would you mind sending me the file? I was wondering if you could move your car, as it is blocking the entrance. Would it be possible to have an answer by the end of today? Notice sending after mind, the past tense in was wondering, and the noun phrase an answer after would it be possible to have.
scenes.say_uz: Mumkin javoblar. Faylni menga yuborib bera olasizmi? Mashinangizni siljita olasizmi deb o‘ylagan edim, u kirishni to‘sib turibdi. Bugun kun oxirigacha javob olish mumkinmi? Mind dan keyin sending, was wondering o‘tgan zamonda.

scenes.title: Obro‘ni saqlash iboralari
board: It is an easy mistake to make.
Perhaps I was not clear.
The system seems to have… · Let us see how we can fix this.
You may not have seen my email.

examples.t: It is an easy detail to miss, so let us check it together.
examples.uz: Bu osongina e’tibordan chetda qoladigan tafsilot, keling, birga tekshiramiz.

examples.t: Perhaps I did not explain that clearly enough.
examples.uz: Balki men buni yetarlicha aniq tushuntirmagandirman.

examples.t: The form seems to have been sent to the wrong address.
examples.uz: Forma noto‘g‘ri manzilga yuborilganga o‘xshaydi.

scenes.say_native: Obro‘ni saqlash tili suhbatdoshning qadr-qimmatini himoya qiladi. Xatoni oddiy holga keltiring: „It is an easy mistake to make.“ Mas’uliyatni bo‘lishing: „Perhaps I was not clear.“ Odamni emas, jarayon yoki vaziyatni ayblang: „The form seems to have gone to the wrong address.“ Chiqish yo‘lini bering: „You may not have seen my email.“ Keyin yechimga o‘ting: „Let us see how we can sort this out.“ „Let us“ — „keling“, bu birgalikdagi ishni bildiradi. O‘zbek madaniyatida „uyat“ va izzat tushunchasi kuchli, shuning uchun bu usul bizga yaqin: boshqalar oldida xijolat qilmaslik. Ingliz ish muhitida ham xuddi shunday, ayniqsa jamoa oldida.
scenes.say: Face-saving language protects the other person's dignity. Normalise the mistake: it is an easy mistake to make. Share responsibility: perhaps I was not clear. Blame the process or situation, not the person: the form seems to have gone to the wrong address. Give a way out: you may not have seen my email. Then move to the fix: let us see how we can sort this out.
scenes.say_uz: Obro‘ni saqlash tili suhbatdoshning qadr-qimmatini himoya qiladi. Xatoni oddiy holga keltiring, mas’uliyatni bo‘lishing, odamni emas jarayonni ayblang, chiqish yo‘lini bering, keyin yechimga o‘ting. Bu usul o‘zbek madaniyatidagi izzat tushunchasiga yaqin.

scenes.title: Xato: ayblov ohangi
board: ✗ You failed to send the form
✓ The form does not seem to have arrived
✗ I told you twice!

examples.t: Let us look at how we can avoid this next time.
examples.uz: Keyingi safar buning oldini qanday olishni ko‘rib chiqaylik.

examples.t: Thanks for flagging it; that is helpful.
examples.uz: Ko‘rsatganingiz uchun rahmat, bu foydali.

scenes.say_native: Ayblov tili odamni sizga qarshi qo‘yadi. „You failed to…“, „I told you twice“, „Why did you not…?“ tinglovchini o‘zini himoya qilishga majbur qiladi. Neytral faktga va umumiy maqsadga o‘ting: „The form does not seem to have arrived, so could we resend it?“ Muammoni xabar qilgan odamni, noqulay bo‘lsa ham, rag‘batlantiring: „Thanks for flagging it.“ Shunda odamlar muammoni yashirmaydi. Iboralar: „flag“ — e’tiborni qaratmoq, „sort out“ — hal qilmoq, „next time“ — keyingi safar. Ayblash vaqtincha yengillik beradi, lekin ishonchni uzoq muddatga buzadi.
scenes.say: Accusation language sets people against you. You failed to, I told you twice and why did you not make the listener defend themselves. Switch to neutral facts and shared goals: the form does not seem to have arrived, so could we resend it? Praise the person who reports a problem, even when it is awkward: thanks for flagging it. That keeps problems visible.
scenes.say_uz: Ayblov tili odamni sizga qarshi qo‘yadi. You failed to, I told you twice kabi iboralar o‘rniga neytral fakt va umumiy maqsadga o‘ting. Muammoni xabar qilgan odamni rag‘batlantiring: thanks for flagging it. Shunda muammolar yashirilmaydi.

scenes.title: Mashq: obro‘ni saqlang
board: 1) You forgot to attach the file.
2) You are late again!
3) Your numbers are wrong.
scenes.say_native: Uchta ayblovni obro‘ni saqlaydigan tilda qayta yozing. Birinchisi: „You forgot to attach the file“. Ikkinchisi: „You are late again!“ Uchinchisi: „Your numbers are wrong“. Xatoni oddiy holga keltiring, mas’uliyatni bo‘lishing yoki jarayonni ayblang va yechimga o‘ting. Javobingizni baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Rewrite three accusations in face-saving language. You forgot to attach the file. You are late again. Your numbers are wrong. Normalise, share responsibility or blame the process, and move to a solution.
scenes.say_uz: Uchta ayblovni obro‘ni saqlaydigan tilda qayta yozing. Siz faylni biriktirishni unutdingiz. Yana kechikdingiz! Raqamlaringiz noto‘g‘ri. Xatoni oddiy holga keltiring, jarayonni ayblang va yechimga o‘ting.

scenes.title: Javoblar: obro‘ni saqlash
board: The attachment seems to be missing. Could you resend it?
I know the traffic has been bad. Shall we start with item two?
Some figures do not seem to match; shall we go through them together?

examples.t: The attachment seems to be missing; could you resend it?
examples.uz: Biriktirilgan fayl yo‘q ko‘rinadi, uni qayta yubora olasizmi?

scenes.say_native: Namunaviy javoblar: „The attachment seems to be missing, so could you resend it?“ „I know the roads have been bad lately. Shall we start with item two while the others arrive?“ „Some of the figures do not seem to match the source, so shall we go through them together?“ Har bir javobda „you“ bilan boshlanadigan ayblov yo‘q, sabab yoki neytral fakt bor va oldinga yo‘l taklif qilinadi. „Shall we“ — „qani, boshlaymizmi“, bu birgalikdagi harakat. Kechikish haqidagi javobda siz sababni tushunayotganingizni ham bildirdingiz, bu odamga yengillik beradi.
scenes.say: Model answers. The attachment seems to be missing, so could you resend it? I know the roads have been bad lately. Shall we start with item two while the others arrive? And: some of the figures do not seem to match the source, so shall we go through them together? Each answer avoids you, offers a reason or a neutral fact, and proposes a way forward.
scenes.say_uz: Namunaviy javoblar. Biriktirilgan fayl yo‘q ko‘rinadi, uni qayta yubora olasizmi? Yo‘llar yomon bo‘lganini bilaman, boshqalar kelguncha ikkinchi bandni boshlaymizmi? Ba’zi raqamlar manbaga mos kelmayotganga o‘xshaydi, birga ko‘rib chiqamizmi?

scenes.title: Tinglash 1: ish natijasi bo‘yicha suhbat
board: Manager: Thanks for the draft. The structure is clear.
Manager: It might be worth shortening the introduction.
Employee: I see. Could you show me which parts?
Manager: Of course. I would start with the second paragraph.
scenes.say_native: Birinchi suhbat — rahbar va xodim. Rahbar: qoralama uchun rahmat, Amir. Tuzilma juda aniq, misollar yaxshi ishlayapti. Ba’zi joylarda biroz uzun, shuning uchun kirishni qisqartirish foydali bo‘lishi mumkin. Xodim: tushundim, qaysi qismlarni ko‘rsata olasiz? Rahbar: albatta, ikkinchi abzasdan boshlardim, qolganini ertaga birga ko‘ramiz. Eshiting: avval ijobiy, keyin „a bit long“, „it might be worth“, „I would start with“ va yechim, birgalikdagi ish.
scenes.say: Thanks for sending the draft, Amir. The structure is very clear, and the examples work well. It is a bit long in places, so it might be worth shortening the introduction. Could you show me which parts? Of course. I would start with the second paragraph, and we can look at the rest together tomorrow.
scenes.say_uz: Qoralama uchun rahmat, Amir. Tuzilma juda aniq, misollar yaxshi ishlayapti. Ba’zi joylarda biroz uzun, shuning uchun kirishni qisqartirish foydali bo‘lishi mumkin. Qaysi qismlarni ko‘rsata olasiz? Albatta. Ikkinchi abzasdan boshlardim, qolganini ertaga birga ko‘ramiz.

scenes.title: Suhbat 1 bo‘yicha savollar
board: 1) What does the manager praise?
2) What does the manager suggest?
3) What will they do tomorrow?
scenes.say_native: Uchta savolga javob bering. Rahbar qaysi ikki narsani maqtaydi? Rahbar nimani taklif qiladi? Ular ertaga nima qiladi? Rahbar qaysi yumshatuvchi iboralarni ishlatganini ham eslang.
scenes.say: Three questions. What two things does the manager praise? What does the manager suggest? And what will they do tomorrow?
scenes.say_uz: Uchta savol. Rahbar qaysi ikki narsani maqtaydi? Rahbar nimani taklif qiladi? Ular ertaga nima qiladi?

scenes.title: Javoblar: suhbat 1
board: structure and examples
shorten the introduction
review the rest together
scenes.say_native: Rahbar aniq tuzilmani va misollarni maqtaydi. Taklif — kirishni qisqartirish, ikkinchi abzasdan boshlash. Ertaga qolganini birga ko‘rib chiqishadi. Rahbar tanqidni „a bit long“ va „it might be worth“ bilan yumshatadi. Ko‘ryapsizmi, bu faqat ohang masalasi emas: aniq ma’lumot ham bor, qaysi qism uzun, nimani qilish kerak. Diplomatik til noaniq til emas: u aniqlikni muloyim shaklda beradi.
scenes.say: The manager praises the clear structure and the examples. The suggestion is to shorten the introduction, starting with the second paragraph. Tomorrow they will go through the rest together. The manager softens the criticism with a bit long and it might be worth.
scenes.say_uz: Rahbar aniq tuzilmani va misollarni maqtaydi. Taklif — kirishni qisqartirish, ikkinchi abzasdan boshlash. Ertaga qolganini birga ko‘rib chiqishadi. Tanqid a bit long va it might be worth bilan yumshatilgan, lekin aniq.

scenes.title: Tinglash 2: mijoz bilan muzokara
board: Client: Could you deliver by Monday?
Supplier: I am afraid Monday is not possible.
Supplier: What I can do is deliver half on Monday.
Client: That would help. Thank you.
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi suhbat — mijoz va yetkazib beruvchi. Mijoz: buyurtmani dushanbagacha olish mumkinmi? Yetkazib beruvchi: afsuski, dushanba real emas, chunki ikkinchi partiya seshanba kuni keladi. Men qila oladigan narsa — yarmini dushanba, qolganini chorshanba yuborish. Bu sizga mosmi? Mijoz: ha, bu juda yordam beradi, yechim topganingiz uchun rahmat. Eshiting: iltimos „would it be possible“, rad „I am afraid“ va sabab, muqobil „what I can do is“, tasdiq „would that work for you“.
scenes.say: Would it be possible to have the order by Monday? I am afraid Monday is not realistic, as the second shipment arrives on Tuesday. What I can do is send half the order on Monday and the rest on Wednesday. Would that work for you? Yes, that would really help. Thank you for finding a solution.
scenes.say_uz: Buyurtmani dushanbagacha olish mumkinmi? Afsuski, dushanba real emas, chunki ikkinchi partiya seshanba kuni keladi. Men buyurtmaning yarmini dushanba, qolganini chorshanba yuborishim mumkin. Bu sizga mosmi? Ha, bu juda yordam beradi. Yechim topganingiz uchun rahmat.

scenes.title: Suhbat 2 bo‘yicha savollar
board: 1) What does the client ask?
2) Why is Monday not realistic?
3) What is the compromise?
scenes.say_native: Savollarga javob bering. Mijoz nimani so‘raydi? Nega dushanba real emas? Yetkazib beruvchi qanday kelishuv taklif qiladi? To‘liq gap bilan, sabab va muqobilni aniq ayting.
scenes.say: Questions. What does the client ask for? Why is Monday not realistic? And what compromise does the supplier offer?
scenes.say_uz: Savollar. Mijoz nimani so‘raydi? Nega dushanba real emas? Yetkazib beruvchi qanday kelishuv taklif qiladi?

scenes.title: Javoblar: suhbat 2
board: order by Monday
second shipment arrives Tuesday
half Monday, rest Wednesday
scenes.say_native: Mijoz buyurtmani dushanbagacha so‘raydi. Dushanba real emas, chunki ikkinchi partiya seshanba kuni keladi. Yetkazib beruvchi kelishuv taklif qiladi: yarmi dushanba, qolgani chorshanba. Rad muloyim, sababli va mijozni qoniqtiradigan muqobil bilan yakunlangan. Bu uch qism darsning markaziy g‘oyasi. Endi hamma narsani birlashtiradigan yakuniy topshiriqqa o‘tamiz.
scenes.say: The client asks for the order by Monday. Monday is not realistic because the second shipment arrives on Tuesday. The supplier offers a compromise: half the order on Monday and the rest on Wednesday. The refusal is polite, reasoned and followed by an alternative that keeps the client happy.
scenes.say_uz: Mijoz buyurtmani dushanbagacha so‘raydi. Dushanba real emas, chunki ikkinchi partiya seshanba kuni keladi. Yetkazib beruvchi yarmini dushanba, qolganini chorshanba taklif qiladi. Rad muloyim, sababli va muqobil bilan.

scenes.title: Yakuniy topshiriq: qiyin vaziyat
board: A colleague’s report has errors and is late.
1) soften the criticism
2) ask for a corrected version
3) agree a new deadline
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy topshiriq. Hamkasbingiz kechikib topshirgan hisobotda bir nechta xato bor. To‘rt-besh gapda tanqidni yumshating, tuzatilgan variantni bilvosita iltimos qiling va yangi muddatni kelishing. Obro‘ni saqlaydigan tildan foydalaning: ayblovsiz, yechimga yo‘naltirilgan. Baland ovozda ayting, keyin namunani eshiting.
scenes.say: Final task. A colleague has handed in a report that is late and has several errors. In four or five sentences, soften the criticism, make an indirect request for a corrected version, and agree on a new deadline, using face-saving language.
scenes.say_uz: Yakuniy topshiriq. Hamkasbingiz kechikib topshirgan hisobotda bir nechta xato bor. To‘rt-besh gapda tanqidni yumshating, tuzatilgan variantni bilvosita iltimos qiling va yangi muddatni kelishing.

scenes.title: Namuna yakuniy javob
board: Thanks for the report. The analysis is strong.
A few figures do not seem to match.
Would you mind sending a corrected version?
Would Thursday work?
scenes.say_native: Namuna: „Thanks for getting the report to me. The analysis is strong, and the conclusions are useful.“ — ijobiy. „A few of the figures do not seem to match the source, which is an easy thing to miss.“ — yumshatilgan tanqid va xatoni oddiy holga keltirish. „Would you mind sending a corrected version?“ — bilvosita iltimos, „mind“ dan keyin „sending“. „I was wondering if Thursday morning would work for you“ — muddat. Kechikish haqida alohida gapirmadik: diplomatiyada ba’zan muhim narsani tanlash ham san’at. Sizning variantingizda shu to‘rt qadam bo‘lsa, topshiriq bajarilgan.
scenes.say: Thanks for getting the report to me. The analysis is strong, and the conclusions are useful. A few of the figures do not seem to match the source, which is an easy thing to miss. Would you mind sending a corrected version? I was wondering if Thursday morning would work for you.
scenes.say_uz: Hisobotni yetkazganingiz uchun rahmat. Tahlil kuchli, xulosalar foydali. Ba’zi raqamlar manbaga mos kelmayotganga o‘xshaydi, buni osongina o‘tkazib yuborish mumkin. Tuzatilgan variantni yuborib bera olasizmi? Payshanba ertalab sizga mos kelishi mumkinmi deb o‘ylagan edim.

scenes.title: Bugungi dars xulosasi
board: hedges · seems · might be worth
I am afraid… but what I can do is…
Would you mind -ing? · I was wondering if…
normalise · share · give a way out
scenes.say_native: Xulosa. Birinchi: tanqidni yumshatish uchun ishga qarating va hedge ishlating. Ikkinchi: rad etishda yumshoq boshlanish, qisqa sabab va muqobil bering. Uchinchi: iltimosni bilvosita tuzing va „would you mind“ dan keyin -ing shaklini unutmang. To‘rtinchi: xatoni oddiy holga keltiring, mas’uliyatni bo‘lishing va chiqish yo‘lini bering. Bu to‘rt usul sizni nafaqat aniq, balki hurmatli ham qiladi.
scenes.say: To sum up, soften criticism by focusing on the work and using hedges. Decline with a soft opening, a short reason and an alternative. Make requests indirect, and remember the -ing form after would you mind. And protect the other person's dignity with face-saving language.
scenes.say_uz: Xulosa. Tanqidni yumshatish uchun ishga qarating va hedge ishlating. Rad etishda yumshoq boshlanish, qisqa sabab va muqobil bering. Iltimosni bilvosita tuzing. Suhbatdoshning obro‘sini saqlang.

scenes.title: Uyga vazifa
board: Rewrite 10 blunt sentences diplomatically
Use at least: 3 hedges · 2 refusals · 3 indirect requests
Success: no accusation, clear meaning
scenes.say_native: Uyga vazifa: o‘nta qo‘pol gapni diplomatik tarzda qayta yozing. Hedge, muloyim rad va bilvosita iltimosdan foydalaning, lekin ma’no aniq qolsin. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: hech qaysi gapda ayblov yo‘q, ma’no aniq va kamida uchta hedge, ikkita rad, uchta bilvosita iltimos ishlatilgan bo‘lsa. Keyingi darsda fikr-mulohaza berish va mojarolarni hal qilishni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Your homework is to rewrite ten blunt sentences diplomatically. Use hedges, polite refusals and indirect requests, and make sure the meaning stays clear. Next lesson: giving feedback and resolving conflicts. Thank you for working hard today.
scenes.say_uz: Uyga vazifangiz: o‘nta qo‘pol gapni diplomatik tarzda qayta yozing. Hedge, muloyim rad va bilvosita iltimosdan foydalaning, lekin ma’no aniq qolsin. Keyingi dars: fikr-mulohaza va mojaroni hal qilish. Bugun yaxshi ishladingiz.

homework_uz: O‘nta qo‘pol gapni diplomatik tarzda qayta yozing: kamida uchta hedge, ikkita muloyim rad va uchta bilvosita iltimos ishlating. Hech qaysi gapda ayblov bo‘lmasin, ma’no aniq qolsin. Keyingi dars: fikr-mulohaza va mojaroni hal qilish.
